kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: 8 dead, hundreds missing as Nepal avalanche triggers flash floods
wire.summary: The disaster is linked to climate change, with experts noting the region's vulnerability to extreme weather.

wire.title: Canada to hit U.S. with retaliatory tariffs. And, remembering music legend Dolly Parton
wire.summary: Canada has announced it plans to hit the U.S. with countertariffs that mirror its actions "dollar for dollar." And, remembering the legacy of country star and icon Dolly Parton, who died at 80.

wire.title: COMIC: 7 lifestyle habits that may boost your chances of getting pregnant
wire.summary: This illustrated guide has evidence-backed advice on how to support fertility for both men and women, including which foods to eat and which activities to avoid.

wire.title: She got an electric bill for $1,373. She's not alone
wire.summary: The price of electricity is soaring in the summer heat, when fans and air conditioners are working nonstop. In Tulsa, Okla., people are having their power cut when they can't pay their bills.

wire.title: Hollywood's summer box office is glowing, but the numbers come with startling caveats
wire.summary: Theaters have had something for everyone this summer, and fans are paying top dollar for premium formats like IMAX. There are also fewer moviegoers, fewer movies and fewer screens than there were pre-COVID.

wire.title: Hospital nursery fire kills 14 newborns in Pakistan's capital, officials order immediate inquiry
wire.summary: A fire erupted early Wednesday in a nursery for newborns at a major government hospital in Pakistan's capital, killing 14 babies, according to hospital officials and the government.

wire.title: Test your global economic knowledge with this quick Planet Money quiz!
wire.summary: Every country tells a different economic story. It's time to test your knowledge of the big ideas we've collected on our World Tour. Eight questions stand between you and your Summer School diploma.

wire.title: Target faces renewed backlash for Halloween costume with 'minstrel show features'
wire.summary: Retailer Target pulled a children's Halloween costume from its shelves after widespread social media backlash, apologizing for selling a garment critics said evoked racist minstrel caricatures.

wire.title: More than 50 kidnapped as violent gang attack in Haiti leaves 47 dead
wire.summary: It is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years, and one gang leader is threatening to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince.

wire.title: Instagram head Adam Mosseri testifies in defense of Meta in child safety trial
wire.summary: The social media giant is being sued by four states who allege it designed Facebook and Instagram to hook kids — and lied to the public about the risks.

wire.title: Door was locked at Pakistan hospital where fire killed 14 babies, witnesses say
wire.summary: A hospital official told the BBC that the door to the ward was not locked, but manned with security guards, to protect the babies.

wire.title: Canada announces 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs on US as high as 50%
wire.summary: The latest escalation in an ongoing trade war between the US and Canada will see new levies on goods from steel to furniture, fresh tuna and makeup.

wire.title: German airport worker dies of malaria after 'mosquito arrives on plane'
wire.summary: Five other airport workers are also receiving treatment following the rare outbreak at German's busiest airport.

wire.title: Far-right Israeli lawmaker damages Palestinian memorial with sledgehammer
wire.summary: Zvi Sukkot's actions have drawn widespread condemnation, including from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

wire.title: Libyan who was cleared after Lockerbie bombing trial dies aged 70
wire.summary: A Facebook post by Libyan Airlines announced the death of Al Amin Khalifah Fhimah and expressed the company's condolences to his family.

wire.title: China advises its citizens to leave Taiwan ally Eswatini over 'security risks'
wire.summary: Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
